comments: The patch meets all three requirements. The `current == 0` early return stops heal from reviving a dead entity, which matches how damage() already treats 0 as dead and never goes below it. `mini(current + amount, max_health)` caps healing at the instance's own max_health and is the correct int-typed Godot 4 builtin, so it raises no engine errors. Healing below the maximum still works, and the existing 50 + 20 = 70 test still covers it. The four new regression tests match the acceptance criteria one for one. In the custom-max test, max_health is set to 40 after _ready, so the clamp goes from 90 straight to 40, which is the expected result. The diff is small and has no dead code, debug prints or unrelated changes. Signatures, class name and file path are unchanged. A small optional point: heal() with a negative amount isn't guarded, but the issue doesn't ask for that.

The health.gd change is correct and meets every requirement. `damaged` is declared with the exact signature. The emitted amount is the health actually lost (`previous - current`), so overkill is clamped correctly. Nothing is emitted for `damage(0)` or after death, `damaged` fires before `died` on a lethal hit, and `heal` and the other signatures are untouched. The new tests cover every acceptance criterion, including signal order on overkill and the second-call parameters. One thing I'd ask to drop: the `.gutconfig.json` edit reformats the `dirs` array for no reason. It also adds `failure_error_types` set to engine/gut/push_error, which I believe is already GUT's default, so the change is probably redundant churn. It does make the 'errors fail tests' criterion explicit, though. Minor and harmless; mergeable.

The patch meets every requirement and stays inside scripts/score_manager.gd. It is still the extends-Node autoload with no class_name, and `var score: int` is unchanged. `combo` starts at 1. The new signature `add_points(n: int, now: float = -1.0)` matches the issue. An untimed call (now omitted or negative) adds `n` unmultiplied and leaves `combo` and the last time alone, so Enemy and the regression tests behave as before. The window is measured from the previous timed call, with `<= 2.0` as specified. A separate `_has_last_time` flag tells a first call apart from a real previous call at t=0.0, which is cleaner than a sentinel value. `reset()` sets score to 0, combo to 1 and forgets the last time. I traced the acceptance cases by hand rather than running them: 60/combo 3, 40/combo 1, 100, and 10/combo 1 after reset all come out right. Nothing in it should raise engine errors or push_error. It uses a named COMBO_WINDOW constant and a short, accurate comment, with no dead code, debug prints or unrelated changes. The only gap is that it adds no tests for the combo behaviour, which the issue doesn't ask for.

The fix is correct. The cooldown is now `1.0 / fire_rate` and is computed on every call, so it follows changes to `fire_rate`. A blocked attempt doesn't update `_last_shot_time`, and the first shot is allowed because `now - (-INF)` is INF. All three acceptance sequences pass, and the existing regression tests are unaffected. `1.0 / 0.0` is float division in GDScript and gives INF, not an engine error. The new tests cover the default rate, a blocked attempt not restarting the cooldown, a changed `fire_rate`, a slow rate and float rounding at the exact interval. The 1e-9 epsilon is documented and only matters for rounding (e.g. 0.35 - 0.1 = 0.2499999...). It does let a shot through up to 1e-9 s early, a small departure from 'at least 1.0 / fire_rate'; a maintainer might ask for a short note on why it's needed. Nitpick: the const sits between the export and the state var. No debug code and no unrelated changes.

The patch meets every requirement. Inventory extends Resource, and add() calls emit_changed() once without redeclaring the `changed` signal. count() returns 0 for items that were never added, and items don't affect each other. Player.inventory is created per instance, so every player starts with its own empty inventory. pickup.tscn has an Area2D root with the script, a CollisionShape2D and a Polygon2D visual. body_entered is connected directly in the scene file, not deferred. The handler checks the body with `as Player`, adds the item and calls queue_free(); it does nothing for any other body. The tests cover every acceptance criterion: the zero default, accumulating counts, the emission count, separate inventories per player, a direct handler call, emitting the signal, and a non-player body. There is no dead code and no debug prints, and the README change is a relevant doc update. One minor note: the typed Dictionary[StringName, int] needs Godot 4.4 or later. That's fine given the vendored GUT 9.7.1.

Meets every requirement. SaveData has the three @export fields. SaveGame extends Node, has no class_name and is registered as an autoload right after ScoreManager. Both methods default the path to "user://save.tres" through a constant. save() fills the score, the Health child's current and an empty inventory, then returns the ResourceSaver.save Error. load_into() calls ResourceLoader.exists first, so a missing file prints no error. It loads with CACHE_MODE_IGNORE so a re-saved file is read fresh, uses `as SaveData` so another resource type returns false without changing anything, and only then writes the score and health. The code is idiomatic, with short useful comments and no dead code or debug prints. The README addition and .uid files are appropriate for Godot 4.4+. The tests cover save contents, restore, re-save freshness, the missing file and the wrong resource type, and they clean up their files. The only small gap is that no test exercises the default path, which is reasonable because such a test would overwrite the real save file.

Meets every requirement. PatrolEnemy extends Enemy and exports waypoints and aggro_range (default 150.0). next_waypoint_index() starts at 0. is_chasing() handles a null target and uses <= with the current values. _physics_process picks one branch per call (chase, patrol or idle), advances the index at most once, wraps to 0 after the last waypoint, leaves the index alone while chasing, idles without errors and always calls move_and_slide(). Enemy._ready is not overridden, so the death scoring and freeing are inherited unchanged. The ARRIVE_DISTANCE constant is cleaner than a magic 4.0. The guard that resets the index when the route is replaced with a shorter one is sensible defensive code, not dead code. The scene inherits enemy.tscn and attaches the new script, so the Health child and other children come along. The Body colour override is a small, reasonable way to tell the two enemies apart. The tests cover every acceptance criterion plus death scoring. The README row and .uid files are appropriate. Nits: aggro_range has no doc comment, unlike waypoints, and the colour tweak was not requested.

Meets every requirement. Health emits health_changed(current, max_health) only when current actually changes. The early return on a dead entity and the existing damage/heal/died behaviour are untouched, including the unclamped heal. ScoreManager emits score_changed after both add_points and reset. The HUD drops _process, sets the score label in _ready and then follows the signal. bind_health sets the label right away and connects for later updates, using the exact "HP: %d/%d" and "Score: %d" formats. HealthLabel sits below ScoreLabel in hud.tscn. The new tests cover all the acceptance criteria, including the method-list check for _process/_physics_process. The README edits and the .uid file are small and relevant. Minor nits: the rebind guard `_health and is_instance_valid(_health) and ...is_connected(...)` is wordier than it needs to be (is_instance_valid alone is enough before the connection check), and rebinding goes slightly beyond what the issue asked for. The placeholder text "HP: 0/0" in the scene is harmless. The ScoreManager connection is never disconnected explicitly, but Godot 4 removes connections automatically when the target object is freed. Clean, idiomatic, mergeable.

The patch meets every requirement. `scripts/events.gd` extends Node, has no class_name, and declares `enemy_died(points: int)` with `@warning_ignore("unused_signal")`. In `project.godot`, `Events` is registered before `ScoreManager`. `Enemy` now emits `Events.enemy_died.emit(points)` and then calls `queue_free()`, and the file no longer mentions ScoreManager. ScoreManager connects once in its own `_ready()` and its handler calls `add_points`, so the score updates synchronously. `reset()` is unchanged and doesn't disconnect the listener. Adding `failure_error_types` (engine/gut/push_error) to `.gutconfig.json` covers the requirement that engine errors and push_error fail the run. The new tests cover each acceptance criterion: autoload order, adding 10 then 25 for a total of 35, the connection owner, killing an enemy (emitted exactly once with [25] and the enemy queued for deletion), and reset keeping the listener. The README update and the `.uid` files are appropriate. One small nit: the `dirs` array in `.gutconfig.json` was reformatted for no reason, which adds diff noise. I haven't run the tests.

The patch meets every requirement. I traced the timing loop by hand against the worked example rather than running it. With _process(0.25) called ten times, the enemy counts come out as 1,2,2,3,3,3,3,4,5,5. wave_finished(0) fires during the 4th call, and wave_finished(1) then all_waves_finished fire during the 9th. A single _process(10.0) spawns all 5 enemies and emits the signals in the right order, with 3 and then 5 Enemy children at each emission. Each next wave's start is based on the last enemy's scheduled time, as specified. Before start(), _process does nothing, start() spawns nothing, and nothing runs after the last wave because _running is cleared. Enemies are added as children at the spawner's origin. target is set before add_child, guarded by the `in` property check, so the enemy's _ready already sees it. The main.tscn edit uses valid Godot 4 syntax (typed-array sub-resources, node_paths for target), keeps the existing nodes and adds exactly one autostarting spawner with two valid waves. The code is small and idiomatic, with no debug prints or dead code; the README rows are a fitting extra. One minor nit: load_steps in the scene header wasn't bumped, but Godot ignores it.

Meets every requirement. Each step is capped at the effect's remaining time, so a single tick(3.0) on a 2 s poison deals exactly 10. Effects at or past their duration are removed at the end of the tick. Two poisons both deal damage and two slows multiply. Poison tracks the total owed and deals only the whole-number part not yet dealt, which gives 2, 3, 2, 3 for 0.5 s ticks. It returns quietly when the target is null or has no Health child, and get_node_or_null with a relative path raises no error on a node outside the tree. Player integration matches the spec: @onready status_effects, effective_speed(), and compute_velocity left as it was. The new scene node and ext_resource are correct, and StatusEffects calls tick only from its own _physics_process. The small EPSILON tolerances guard against float drift and don't change any of the specified results, though strictly they bend the 'exact rule' a little. The code is idiomatic, with typed arrays, doc comments and no debug output. The README update and new tests are relevant and cover the acceptance criteria. Minor nit: parallel _effects/_elapsed arrays could be one array of small records, but that's fine as it is.

The fix is correct and minimal: the cooldown check now uses `1.0 / fire_rate`, so exactly one interval later is allowed, and blocked attempts don't restart the cooldown. `reset()` sets the last-shot time back to -INF, which clears the cooldown, allows any time (including one earlier than the last shot), leaves `fire_rate` alone and is harmless on a weapon that has never fired. The tests use only the public API, use binary-exact times, free the weapon with `add_child_autofree`, and use no `await` or real time. Each broken version fails at least one test. The boundary off-by-one fails `test_default_fire_rate_is_shots_per_second` and `test_shot_exactly_at_cooldown_boundary_is_allowed`. A `reset()` that doesn't clear fails `test_reset_allows_immediate_shot_at_same_time` and `test_reset_allows_shot_earlier_than_last_shot`. Treating `fire_rate` as seconds fails the 0.25 s and four-shots tests. Every acceptance case is covered, and nothing unrelated is changed apart from the expected Godot `.uid` file. Small nit: the test file is somewhat redundant. For example, `test_first_shot_always_allowed` repeats checks made elsewhere, and several reset tests overlap. It could be trimmed, but that isn't a reason to block the merge.
